newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire acknowledges fall of town of Isiro to rebels.
newsitem.headline: Zaire acknowledges fall of town of Isiro to rebels.

text.p: Zaire's army said on Thursday that the key town of Isiro had fallen to rebels after two days of fierce fighting and that it planned to reinforce Kisangani, headquarters for its military operations in the war zone.

"Isiro was taken by the rebels last night, after two days of heavy fighting. The rebels are now reported to be moving west towards Buta," a senior Zairean defence ministry official told Reuters. The rebels say Isiro fell on Tuesday.
Isiro is 340 km (210 miles) north east of Kisangani, staging post for a counter-offensive that the army launched on January 20 and a declared target of rebel leader Laurent Kabila.
"We are planning to send more fresh troops into Kisangani over the weekend. The situation necessitates reinforcements," the Zairean official said.
Isiro is about 800 km (500 miles) east of ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko's jungle palace at Gbadolite, another declared target of the rebels. Buta is 450 km (280 miles) east of Gbadolite.
